Each recurring cause (two or more runs or incidents) has an item, existing or new, linked here; the linked items are the fixes that trunk-red-rate-target-20261024 waits for

Evidence needed for the classification (logs, job records, attempt history) is saved on or linked from this item before it expires (artifacts have 7-, 14- or 30-day retention, so some evidence may already be gone)

# Trunk red-run classification, 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-24

Tracker item: `trunk-red-run-triage-20261024`. Analysis only; no repository change. Evidence: see section 8.

## 1. Scope and counts

- Window (UTC): start 2026-10-10T00:00:00Z, end 2026-10-24T23:59:59Z, selected by run `created_at`. First run 38013156721 (2026-10-10T01:26:02Z), last run 40143062585 (2026-10-24T23:31:06Z). Workflow `trunk.yml`, branch `develop`, event `push`. All 490 runs were completed.
- 490 Trunk push runs, 489 distinct head SHAs (runs 38911870169 and 38911871641 share one SHA). 427 latest-attempt success, 63 latest-attempt failure.
- The tracker's original capture (466 runs, 59 failures) ends at run 40110069777 (a56738db4, 2026-10-24T16:07:08Z). Four more red runs (the chDB incident, INC-16) landed after that cutoff, giving 63. The two runs the capture called still red (40071232825, 40071524792) are no longer the newest: both were cleared by fix-forward #3385.
- Attempt history exists for every run: only 3 runs have more than one attempt (38144726540: red, red; 39615662898: red, green; 39794975920: red, green). No attempt was cancelled.
- Runs with any red attempt: **65** (63 latest-red + 2 whose first attempt was red and rerun green). Red attempts: 66. Any-red rate 65/490 = 13.3%; latest-attempt red rate 63/490 = 12.9%; first-attempt red 65/490 = 13.3% (all 3 multi-attempt runs started red, so first-attempt and any-attempt coincide).
- Passing-on-rerun runs (2) show intermittency only; both are the producer-check failure (INC-12). Reruns elsewhere: none.
- Failing job by attempt: `fast (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)` 17 attempts, medium-test shards 43 attempts (many with several shards red at once), `dist-artifact` 6 attempts (all `Bind distributions to the producer attempt`). No macOS, Windows or non-3.12 job ever failed in Trunk.
- The 65 runs collapse into **16 incidents** (same signature and culprit, or one recurring signature). 33 of the 65 runs are later runs that only carried a defect already red in an earlier run; 12 are independent flake hits (INC-03).

### Counts by recovery (runs)

| Recovery | Runs | Incidents |
|---|---|---|
| Fix-forward | 33 | INC-02, 06, 08, 10, 11, 14, 15 |
| Revert | 10 | INC-09 (#3061), INC-13 (#3190), INC-16 (#3422) |
| None (cleared by a later green run with no change) | 20 | INC-01, 03, 04, 05, 07 (16 runs) and 4 of 6 INC-12 runs |
| Rerun | 2 | INC-12 |

Reds therefore mostly cleared by a code change, not by luck: 43 of 65 runs trace to a fix-forward or revert. Only 3 incidents were reverted; fix-forward was the norm. Two more fixes (#3095 amplab, #3413 producer check) landed after those flakes had already stopped or recurred.

## 4. Stale-base composition versus the governance threshold

Source: `docs/internal/merge-queue-governance.md:214-216` ("If a trunk failure traces to a pull request that was green on an older base more than about once a week, the owner should consider reinstating the strict up-to-date rule and its refresh cost."). Rulesets currently have `strict_required_status_checks_policy` false and no merge queue.

Method: a stale-base composition incident is one where a PR was green on its older base and the failure appears only because of a commit merged after that base (the test or code interacting with the later commit). Checked by diffing each culprit's base, merge parent and PR check runs. "Behind" counts commits between the PR's recorded base and its merge parent (PR API `base.sha`, approximate).

Only one incident meets that definition: INC-06 (#2985 vs #2980, confidence high).

| Week | INC-06 | Other composition incidents | Independent stale-base count | vs ~1/week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 10 to 16 (186 runs, 43 red) | 1 | 0 | 1 | at threshold (not above) |
| Oct 17 to 23 (258 runs, 14 red) | 0 | 0 | 0 | below |
| Oct 24 (46 runs, 6 red) | 0 | 0 | 0 | below |
| ISO W41 (Oct 10 to 11) / W42 (Oct 12 to 18) / W43 (Oct 19 to 25) | 0 / 1 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 1 / 0 | below or at |

Whole window: 1 incident in 15 days is about 0.47 per week. **The threshold is not exceeded under the composition definition, so this window does not by itself trigger an owner review of reinstating the up-to-date rule.** The remaining 15 incidents are not stale-base: 4 flaky/unknown, 1 API, 9 genuine defects whose culprit PRs were already broken against the base they merged on (they were green pre-merge only because the PR lane skipped the failing test or does not run the Trunk lane's environment).

Sensitivity. If the governance sentence is read literally ("a PR green on an older base", i.e. any culprit PR behind its base at merge), 9 incidents qualify (INC-02 #2821 13 behind, INC-06 #2985 9, INC-08 #3018 1, INC-09 #3049 2, INC-10 #3066 4, INC-11 #3122 1, INC-14 #3200 21, INC-15 #3378 1, INC-16 #3400 12), about 4.2 per week, which exceeds the threshold. Rebasing would not have prevented 8 of them: the failing test already existed in the base and the PR lane skipped it (INC-08, 10, 11), the Trunk lane's environment or placement differs from the PR lane (INC-02, 14, 16), or the defect was in the PR itself (INC-09, 15). Only INC-06 depended on the missing commit. INC-13 was up to date at merge. Decision for the owner: adopt the narrow definition (no review) or the literal one (review requested). I recommend recording the narrow definition in the governance doc so the threshold measures what refresh would fix.

## 5. How the red-trunk and arm gates treated these runs

Gate behavior (read from `scripts/trunk_revert.py` and the governance doc, not from gate logs; no gate execution records were available):

- `make pr-open` (`trunk_gate`; `scripts/trunk_revert.py` exists since 2026-10-03, so it was present for the whole window): refuses non-revert branches once the **newest** `trunk.yml` run on develop finished red more than 30 minutes ago. It does not block while a newer run is in progress, nor when `gh` cannot read runs, and revert branches are exempt. Only the newest run is examined, and only at open time.
- `make pr-arm*` (`arm_gate`, from #3215, 2026-10-21T04:08Z): refuses at once while the newest completed run is red and no revert of its culprit is on develop. Until #3415 (2026-10-25T01:15Z, after the window) it blamed the newest red run, not the first, so it named the wrong culprit and refused the real culprit's revert (`trunk-arm-gate-blames-newest-red-run-20261022`). PRs armed before the run failed still merge, and arming outside those targets bypasses it.

Effect on the window (merge time approximated by run created time; arming time not recorded):

- 48 merges (of 489 non-first runs) were created while the newest *completed* run was red: 29 within the 30-minute grace and 19 more than 30 minutes after. Of those 48, 18 carried the same red defect (14 within grace, 4 beyond) and 30 were green. Of the 19 beyond grace, 6 were fixes or reverts (#2907, #2995, #3127, the #3185 revert, #3222, #3385), 4 carried the defect, and 9 were unrelated green PRs. So non-fix PRs did merge more than 30 minutes into a red tip (13 of 19), either armed or opened earlier, or through a bypass; the records do not say which.
- The grace and in-progress rules exclude fast bursts. INC-06, 08, 09, 10 and 16 each had 4 to 9 red runs inside 1 to 3 hours: merges arrived every 5 to 30 minutes, each run took 10 to 45 minutes, so the newest completed run was usually in the grace window or newer runs were in progress. The pr-open gate would rarely have refused during these bursts.
- "Newest run" semantics explain much of why reds clear without a revert: any green run on a later sha lifts both gates, even when it is a flake (INC-03: 12 reds interleaved with 12 greens), an unrelated PR or the fix-forward itself. Only INC-09, 13 and 16 were reverted (10 runs). Fix-forward cleared 7 incidents (33 runs); 20 runs cleared with no change at all (flakes and the producer check), and 2 by rerun. The three reverts took 1.2 to 3.0 h; fix-forwards took 2.3 to 12.1 h (median 8.8 h).
- The arm gate was in force for INC-12 (10-21, 10-22), INC-14, INC-15 and INC-16. The record does not show an arm refusal tied to any of them: INC-15's culprit's successor #3379 merged four minutes after the first red run began, before the gate could see a completed red.

Not established: whether any PR was refused or bypassed by the gates (no gate logs). See the unknowns.
